title: Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe Won't Start (crash) due to RPCRT4.dll
author: evanly
summary: Command Palette crashes in RPCRT4.dll after reboot but launches again after toggling the module off and on, suggesting a boot-time RPC/extension initialization failure rather than permanent package corruption.

confidence.rationale: The recovery pattern strongly implicates startup state, but RPCRT4 is a broad fault location and the exact owner requires a cold-boot trace.

judgment.rationale: The report includes repeatable reboot steps, Event Viewer fault data, a diagnostic ZIP, and independent confirmation on a newer CmdPal package. Maintainer-side startup tracing is the next useful step.
evidence: The crash occurs after reboot and temporarily clears after PowerToys update or toggling Command Palette off/on.
Event Viewer reports Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe faulting in RPCRT4.dll with exception 0xc0020043.
A second user confirms the same pattern on CmdPal executable 0.11.2606.25002 and package 0.11.11762.0.
judgment.recommended_action: Trace cold-boot RPC/extension startup and add recovery when the initial app-service/RPC connection is invalid.

fix_assessment.rationale: No active merged fix covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path. The evidence supports a bounded design hypothesis, but the exact failing RPC call requires a maintainer cold-boot trace or dump. The dashboard should offer that reproduction rather than ask reporters to perform internal profiling.

proposed_fixes.title: Recover Command Palette from invalid cold-boot RPC initialization
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Command Palette appears to initialize an RPC/app-service or extension connection into an invalid state during logon; toggling the module rebuilds that state and restores launch.
plan: Instrument cold-boot initialization boundaries around CmdPal UI activation, host connection, and extension enumeration to identify the RPC call preceding 0xc0020043.
Validate connection/endpoint state before first use and recreate the client/host channel once when startup returns a terminal RPC failure.
Add lifecycle coverage for boot/logon activation, delayed dependency availability, and module off/on restart without masking repeated faults.
verification: Reboot a machine with Command Palette enabled and confirm the first shortcut launch succeeds repeatedly.
Simulate unavailable/delayed host or extension endpoints and verify one bounded recovery attempt without a crash loop.

confidence.rationale: The recovery pattern strongly implicates startup state, but RPCRT4 is a broad fault location and the exact owner requires a cold-boot trace.

issue_context.summary: Command Palette crashes in RPCRT4.dll after reboot but launches again after toggling the module off and on, suggesting a boot-time RPC/extension initialization failure rather than permanent package corruption.

No assignee or linked fix appears in the issue timeline.
inferences: A startup ordering or stale RPC/app-service endpoint may be established during logon and reset by toggling the module.
The RPCRT4 fault alone does not identify which Command Palette component owns the invalid state.

reproduce.title: Capture Command Palette cold-boot initialization failure
reproduce.version_requirement: Current stable PowerToys release unless the issue names a required preview build
prerequisites: Command Palette enabled at Windows sign-in
setup: Confirm Command Palette launches before reboot.
Enable startup and reboot the machine normally.
steps: After sign-in, invoke Command Palette once with its shortcut.
Record whether Microsoft.CmdPal.UI.exe starts and the exact Event Viewer timestamp/exception.
Without reinstalling, toggle Command Palette off and on and invoke it again.
Capture a maintainer trace or dump around the first RPC/host/extension initialization when possible.
reproduce.expected_result: Command Palette should launch on the first post-reboot invocation; a failed connection should be recovered or reported without an RPCRT4 crash.
